newsitem.title: GERMANY: German stocks end listless bourse trade lower.
newsitem.headline: German stocks end listless bourse trade lower.

text.p: German shares were generally lower as bourse trade ended on Friday after sentiment was hit by weakness on Wall Street and a marginally softer dollar.
The DAX index, which tracks trade in 30 blue-chip German stocks, ended at 3,184.09 points, down 11.94 points or 0.37 percent, off earlier lows at 3,171.05 points.
"There seems to be wholesale selling across the board this morning and the big heavyweights, like the chemical companies and Daimler Benz AG, are all down," said one Frankfurt trader.
Increased volatility ahead of an options expiry later also impacted on trading sentiment, and there was further discussion among market players of an imminent correction.

"It's difficult to find anyone bullish at the moment, on say the United States for example. This acts as a kind of buffer against market collapse as people have adjusted their positions already," the trader said.
"There is always the possibility of a sharp decline, but there is no evidence in the fundamentals to suggest that could happen," he said.
Among shares on the rise was Viag AG, which ended bourse up 16 marks at 704.50 marks after Goldman Sachs upgraded the stock to "outperformer".
Sportswear manufacturer Puma AG rose nearly eight percent in electronic trade after what looked like upbeat 1996 figures.

However, the share ended bourse trade down 2.50 marks at 60.50 marks as dealers said the figures were worse than they had expected as the net profit figure of 83.8 million marks including an extraordinary gain of 24.1 million marks..
Drugs company Schering AG ended at 144.90 marks, up 2.95 marks, after an upgrade by investment house Dresdner Kleinwort Benson from "trading buy" to "buy".
